name: Kentucky Eats: Restaurants
subtitle: Hot Browns, Burgoo & Bourbon
description:
Kentucky's restaurants, from a Hot Brown at the hotel that created it to mutton and burgoo in Owensboro.

Kentucky Eats is a free guide to eating in Kentucky: 9 places for a Hot Brown, 6 Kentucky classics from burgoo to beer cheese, 8 tables in Bardstown and bourbon country, 9 Covington and Newport picks and 4 historic inns and taverns we checked by hand, plus 9,841 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 420 towns, from Louisville and Lexington to Paducah and Pikeville. No account, no ads.

KENTUCKY GUIDES
• Hot Browns: from the Brown Hotel, where the dish was created in 1926, to Frankfort's Hot Brown Trail.
• Kentucky Classics: Owensboro mutton and burgoo, beer cheese, rolled oysters and spoonbread.
• Bardstown & Bourbon Country: dinner between distillery tours.
• Covington & Newport: goetta, a German beer hall and river-town dining.
• Historic Inns & Taverns: from 1779 to the Beaumont Inn.
• James Beard Honors and Oldest Places.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "hot brown", "bardstown", "moonlite".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a dated 2025 or 2026 source or a Kentucky tourism office's own page. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept by the reliability rule tested in the states that publish official restaurant lists, plus Louisville Metro's permitted restaurants. 6,267 places show their latest official inspection score, as published and dated: 4,696 from county health departments on Kentucky's public inspection portal and 1,571 from Louisville Metro's open data, with Louisville's own A, B or C grade where it gave one. Louisville places with no published result link to Louisville Metro's food safety page. 1,551 places are marked "Serves alcohol" from Kentucky ABC's on-premises licenses and Louisville Metro's; a place with no matched license shows it as unknown, never no. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the Kentucky Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Kentucky ABC, Louisville Metro Government or any health department), the Kentucky Distillers' Association, or the James Beard Foundation. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; inspection scores from Louisville Metro Open Data (public domain, PDDL) and Kentucky's public inspection portal; alcohol licenses from Kentucky ABC and Louisville Metro. Sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Kentucky Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Kentucky (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: Hot Browns, Kentucky classics (burgoo, mutton, beer cheese), Bardstown and bourbon-country dining, Covington and Newport, and historic inns, 34 places checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus the James Beard Foundation's honorees. It also lists 9,841 restaurants, cafés and bars in 420 towns from open map data and Louisville Metro's open records. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Hot Browns (or Kentucky Classics, Bardstown & Bourbon Country, Covington & Newport, Historic Inns & Taverns, James Beard Honors, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; further down are the latest official inspection score with its date (Louisville Metro's, with its letter grade where it gave one, or the county's from Kentucky's public portal), a link to that source in Safari, and "Serves alcohol" where a Kentucky ABC or Louisville Metro license matches.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("hot brown", "bardstown", "moonlite").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Outside Kentucky (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Kentucky; distance sorting still works.

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the Kentucky Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); Louisville Metro's food permits, inspections and alcohol licenses (Louisville Metro Open Data, public domain under the PDDL); county inspection scores from Kentucky's public inspection portal; Kentucky ABC's on-premises drink licenses (name and address only); James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites, local news and official tourism pages.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/kentucky-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Kentucky; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. Inspection scores are shown as Louisville Metro and Kentucky's county health departments published them, with the date; the app computes no grades and ranks nothing by inspections. "Serves alcohol" comes only from Kentucky ABC's and Louisville Metro's license records. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or the James Beard Foundation.
